corrected_value.authors: Jiang, Y., Costello, P., & He, S.
corrected_value.title: Processing of invisible stimuli: Advantage of upright faces and recognizable words in overcoming interocular suppression.

decisions.location: Method / Control experiment (lines 285-299); Statistical analysis (lines 435-443); Results / Control experiment (lines 515-527); References (lines 651-653)
decisions.quote:
The statistical tests
themselves were equivalent across both experiments, only the condition changed: congruent
was replaced by upright and incongruent by inverted. The sole difference was that we used
the t-value and sample size reported by Jiang et al. (2007) to determine BFr0 (respectively,
5.53 and 10).
decisions.reason: In addition to replicating Hung, Styles, & Hsieh (2017) (shipped row 2517, DOI 10.1177/0956797616677313) in the main experiment, the authors conducted an empirical control experiment with the same participants testing whether upright faces break continuous flash suppression (CFS) faster than inverted faces, directly replicating the face-inversion suppression effect of Jiang, Costello, & He (2007) and computing a replication Bayes factor (BFr0 = 0.43) using the t-value (5.53) and sample size (10) reported by Jiang et al. (2007). Jiang et al. (2007) (DOI 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2007.01902.x) is a distinct original work from Hung et al. (2017) and is completely absent from the shipped rows.
